sources.title: Aaron D. Wyner and Jacob Ziv, “The Rate-Distortion Function for Source Coding with Side Information at the Decoder”
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete 10-page IEEE Transactions on Information Theory paper PDF, author-hosted; full text inspected.
sources.locator: §I problem statement, Theorem 1 and Remarks 3–6, printed pp. 1–3; §III converse, pp. 6–7; §IV direct theorem and proof, pp. 7–9; Appendix Theorem A2, pp. 9–10.
sources.read_locator: Inspected the complete paper and the full argument in §§III–IV and Appendix Theorem A2. The original uses base-2 rates, finite alphabets, expected distortion, and an auxiliary satisfying Y–Z conditional independence given X; the local carriers state natural-log nats and prove their own finite-alphabet route.
sources.extent: Primary historical treatment of the exact finite-alphabet decoder-only-side-information theorem. Its operational model and assumptions match the local finite, bounded-distortion specialization; no source proof is substituted for the complete local arguments.
sources.support: Finite Wyner–Ziv theorem, converse/achievability structure, lossless endpoint, cardinality, convexity, continuity, and the no-rate-loss criterion noted for plan reconciliation.

contents.name: §I-B formal decoder-only side-information model and finite auxiliary test channel
contents.reason: The local definition fixes finite alphabets, deterministic block maps, expected normalized additive distortion, nats, and the encoder/decoder observation split.

contents.name: §I-C Theorem 1: exact finite-alphabet Wyner–Ziv characterization
contents.reason: The local theorem proves the finite bounded-distortion operational equality with decoder-only Y and supplies the converse and binning achievability arguments in full.

contents.name: §III Theorem 2 and converse single-letterization
contents.reason: The source converse motivates the claim; the local proof separately justifies its conditional-mutual-information single-letterization and operational limit.

contents.name: §IV Theorem 4 and direct random-codebook/binning argument
contents.reason: The source uses typical codewords and random binning; the local proof gives complete covering, selected-codeword Markov typicality, packing, bounded-distortion, and deterministic-selection steps.
contents.locator: §IV, Lemma 5 and Theorem 4 proof, printed pp. 7–9.

contents.name: Appendix Theorem A2: convexity, continuity, cardinality, and attainment
contents.reason: The local posterior-vector reduction proves the |U|≤|X|+1 bound and finite-dimensional attainment; the separate continuity item proves the endpoint claims locally.

contents.name: §I, equation (6) and Remark 3: lossless endpoint H(X|Y)
contents.reason: The local zero-Hamming-distortion calculation is complete and is compared with the exact two-source Slepian–Wolf corner.

contents.name: §I, Remark 5: sufficient criterion for no rate loss when the encoder also knows Y
contents.reason: The broader track prose proposes this criterion, but the registered plan-spec summary commissions the finite Wyner–Ziv theorem, cardinality, and Berger–Tung inner bound only; the mismatch is recorded for owner scope reconciliation.

contents.name: §II doubly symmetric binary source closed-form evaluation
contents.reason: The assigned examples are the no-side-information identity and lossless endpoints; the detailed binary-source closed form is not required by the registered plan-spec summary.

sources.title: Abbas El Gamal and Young-Han Kim, Network Information Theory, author lecture notes
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete author lecture-note PDF retrieved from arXiv and extracted for the relevant full lectures and appendices.
sources.locator: Chapter 2 typical sequences and method of types; Lecture 12, Wyner–Ziv theorem and proof; Lecture 13, Markov lemma, mutual packing lemma, and Berger–Tung inner bound; Appendix B selected-codeword/Markov-lemma arguments.
sources.read_locator: Read the full relevant Lecture 12 and Lecture 13 sections and the cited Appendix B lemma proofs. The local arguments retain finite alphabets, support restrictions, nats, independent marginal codebooks, independent bin labels, and the exact Markov factorization.
sources.extent: Independent full lecture-note treatment of both the exact single-encoder theorem and the multiterminal inner bound. The local items state and prove the finite helper lemmas rather than treating the lecture notes as an unproved dependency.
sources.support: Typical/type-class conventions, WZ covering and binning route, Markov typicality, random-bin packing, and Berger–Tung subset inequalities.

contents.name: Chapter 2: finite typical sequences and method-of-types cardinality estimates
contents.reason: The local definition fixes a support-restricted relative-frequency convention needed by its finite type proofs.
contents.locator: Chapter 2, typical sequences and method of types.

contents.name: Chapter 2: exponential type-class cardinality bounds
contents.reason: The local lemma proves both type-class bounds, including zero coordinates, from finite product probabilities and a mode argument.
contents.locator: Chapter 2, typical sequences and type-class bounds.

contents.name: Lecture 12: WZ codebook covering and first jointly typical selected codeword
contents.reason: The local proof derives a uniform conditional-type lower bound and the exact first-success selected-word law for finite alphabets.

contents.name: Lecture 12: Wyner–Ziv random binning and decoder-side typicality packing
contents.reason: The local packing lemma gives the full finite-subset type-fan count, marginal likelihood bound, independent bin-collision calculation, and union bound.
contents.locator: Lecture 12, Wyner–Ziv direct theorem and packing analysis.

contents.name: Lecture 12: finite-alphabet Wyner–Ziv theorem
contents.reason: The theorem carrier supplies a complete local operational converse and covering/binning achievability proof under the stated finite bounded-distortion hypotheses.

contents.name: Lecture 13 and Appendix B: selected-codeword Markov lemma
contents.reason: The local finite conditional-type proof supplies an explicit hypergeometric variance bound and a uniform finite-union argument.
contents.locator: Lecture 13 Markov lemma; Appendix B selected-codeword and Markov-lemma proofs.

contents.name: Lecture 13: mutual packing lemma for independent marginal codebooks
contents.reason: The local packing lemma specializes the mutual-packing calculation with explicit independence from the source and independent bin labels.
contents.locator: Lecture 13, mutual packing lemma and error analysis.

contents.name: Lecture 13: finite-alphabet Berger–Tung inner bound
contents.reason: The local theorem states the k-terminal subset inequalities and proves only achievability, preserving the inner-bound-only caveat.
contents.locator: Lecture 13, theorem and full covering/Markov/packing proof, pp. 3–13.

contents.name: Lecture 13: lossless Slepian–Wolf special case with identity auxiliaries
contents.reason: The B example calculates the identity-auxiliary inequalities and invokes the exact finite-IID Slepian–Wolf theorem only for this lossless case.
contents.locator: Lecture 13, finite Berger–Tung theorem and lossless specialization.

sources.title: João Barros, Reachback Communication in Wireless Sensor Networks, doctoral dissertation
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete author-hosted 168-page dissertation PDF fetched and extracted; the full relevant chapter section and cited Markov lemma inspected.
sources.locator: Chapter 2, §2.2.3, Lemma 2.3 (Markov Lemma); Chapter 4, §4.2.1, “A Simple Proof for the Berger–Tung Inner Bound,” printed pp. 66–72.
sources.read_locator: Read the complete Chapter 4 §4.2.1 two-stage quantize/Slepian–Wolf proof and the full Chapter 2 §2.2.3 Markov-lemma statement and proof. The dissertation’s worked inner-bound proof is two-terminal; it is used as an independent treatment of that case, while the local proof establishes general finite k.
sources.extent: Independent dissertation treatment of Berger–Tung and conditional typicality. Its two-terminal scope is not used to justify the local k-terminal extension.
sources.support: Independent quantize-and-bin proof structure and Markov-lemma interface for the finite multiterminal theorem and its supporting lemmas.

contents.name: Chapter 2 §2.2.3, Lemma 2.3: Markov typicality for a conditionally generated sequence
contents.reason: The local proof verifies the finite conditional-type-uniform case directly with hypergeometric counts rather than importing a general typicality assertion.

contents.name: Chapter 4 §4.2.1, Theorem 4.2: two-terminal Berger–Tung inner bound
contents.reason: This is an independent two-terminal treatment; the local theorem extends the proof to arbitrary finite k and expressly keeps the conclusion as an inner bound.

contents.name: Chapter 4 §4.2.1: separate rate-distortion quantization followed by Slepian–Wolf binning
contents.reason: The local code construction uses independent auxiliary codebooks and binning, and proves the full k-terminal subset packing bounds.

contents.name: Chapter 4 §4.2.1: jointly typical codeword selection in finite rate-distortion codebooks
contents.reason: The local type-count proof supplies a quantitative covering estimate and the conditional-type law of the first selected codeword.

contents.name: Chapter 4 §4.2.1: lossless bin decoding of the quantization indices
contents.reason: The local packing lemma supplies an all-subset false-tuple count for independent bins and finite alphabets.

sources.locator: Chapter 10 §10.2, finite rate-distortion; Chapter 11 §11.1, Theorem 11.1.3; Chapter 15 §§15.2, 15.4.1–15.4.3, and 15.9, printed pp. 520–523, 549–556, and 580–586.

sources.extent: Independent textbook treatment. The WZ direct proof is explicitly an outline with a pointer to Wyner–Ziv for details; the local item therefore proves every coding step in full.
